\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ای} \fa{کاش} (ey kâsh)}{ای کاش (ey kâsh)}]{\fa{ای} \fa{کاش} (ey kâsh) — if only, I wish}

\label{lesson:FA-C394-ey-kash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to make sure, then the Persian for apparently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ای} \fa{کاش}}
\textbf{\fa{ای} \fa{کاش}} (\emph{ey kâsh}) — \textquotedblleft{}if only, I wish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ای} \fa{کاش} \fa{وقت} \fa{بیشتری} \fa{داشتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ey kâsh vaqt-e bishtari dâshtam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If only I had more time.
\end{quote}

It takes the past for a wish about now: \emph{ey kâsh dâshtam}. \emph{Kâsh} alone means the same.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ای} \fa{کاش}} is native Persian, built from \emph{ey} \textquotedblleft{}oh\textquotedblright{}, the calling word, + \emph{kâsh} \textquotedblleft{}would that\textquotedblright{}. The origin of \emph{kâsh} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ey kâsh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ey kâsh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ey kâsh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to make sure, then the Persian for apparently, then say \emph{ey kâsh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ارزیابی} \fa{کردن} (arzyâbi kardan)}{ارزیابی کردن (arzyâbi kardan)}]{\fa{ارزیابی} \fa{کردن} (arzyâbi kardan) — to assess, to evaluate}

\label{lesson:FA-C394-arzyabi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for apparently, then the Persian for if only.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ارزیابی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{ارزیابی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{arzyâbi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to assess, to evaluate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{معلم} \fa{کار} \fa{هر} \fa{دانش} \fa{آموز} \fa{را} \fa{ارزیابی} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mo'allem kâr-e har dânesh âmuz râ arzyâbi mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher assesses each pupil's work.
\end{quote}

\emph{Arz} \textquotedblleft{}worth\textquotedblright{} + \emph{yâbi} \textquotedblleft{}finding\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{yâftan}, + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ارزیابی}} is a modern native coinage built from \emph{arz} \textquotedblleft{}worth\textquotedblright{}, the stem behind \emph{arzesh} \textquotedblleft{}value\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{yâbi} \textquotedblleft{}finding\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{yâb-}, the present stem of \emph{yâftan} \textquotedblleft{}to find\textquotedblright{}. To assess is to find the worth.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arzyâbi kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{arzyâbi kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for apparently, then the Persian for if only, then say \emph{arzyâbi kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تضمین} \fa{کردن} (tazmin kardan)}{تضمین کردن (tazmin kardan)}]{\fa{تضمین} \fa{کردن} (tazmin kardan) — to guarantee}

\label{lesson:FA-C394-tazmin-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for if only, then the Persian for to assess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تضمین} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تضمین} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tazmin kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to guarantee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هیچ} \fa{کس} \fa{نمیتواند} \fa{موفقیت} \fa{را} \fa{تضمین} \fa{کند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hich kas nemitavânad movaffaqiyat râ tazmin konad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Nobody can guarantee success.
\end{quote}

\emph{Tazmin} \textquotedblleft{}guarantee\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تضمین}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{taḍmīn} \textquotedblleft{}guaranteeing\textquotedblright{}; Persian says the Arabic \emph{ḍ} as \emph{z}. \emph{Kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ریسک} (risk)}{ریسک (risk)}]{\fa{ریسک} (risk) — a risk}

\label{lesson:FA-C394-risk}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to assess, then the Persian for to guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ریسک}}
\textbf{\fa{ریسک}} (\emph{risk}) — \textquotedblleft{}a risk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{کار} \fa{ریسک} \fa{زیادی} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in kâr risk-e ziyâdi dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is very risky.
\end{quote}

A European loan; \emph{risk kardan} — to take a risk.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ریسک}} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{risque} \textquotedblleft{}risk\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خطر} \fa{کردن} (khatar kardan)}{خطر کردن (khatar kardan)}]{\fa{خطر} \fa{کردن} (khatar kardan) — to take a risk}

\label{lesson:FA-C394-khatar-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to guarantee, then the Persian for a risk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خطر} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خطر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khatar kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to take a risk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{خطر} \fa{کرد} \fa{و} \fa{شغلش} \fa{را} \fa{عوض} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u khatar kard va shoghlash râ 'avaz kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He took a risk and changed his job.
\end{quote}

\emph{Khatar} \textquotedblleft{}danger\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. Literary; everyday speech says \emph{risk kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{خطر}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{khaṭar} \textquotedblleft{}danger\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); with the inherited Persian verb \emph{kardan} it means to face the danger.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
